questions.stem: All are true regarding trichomoniasis except:

options.label: D
options.text: Sexual mode is the most common method of transmission

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B. Reservoir for infection is lice

Ans. B. Promastigote

 

Kala-azar is caused by Leishmania donovani, and its life cycle involves two key forms:

  1. Promastigote (flagellated form)
    1. Found in the gut of the sandfly (vector)
    2. Infective stage for humans
    3. Transmitted via the bite of an infected female sandfly
  2. Amastigote (non-flagellated form)
    1. Intracellular form inside human macrophages
    2. Diagnostic stage in humans (seen in bone marrow, spleen, etc.)
       

Other options:

 

Option A. Amastigotes: Diagnostic form in humans, not infective stage.

 

Option C. Trypomastigote: Infective form of Trypanosoma, not Leishmania.

 

Option D. Epimastigote: Seen in Trypanosoma life cycle, not in Leishmania.

 

Educational Objective: 

 

Promastigotes are the infective stage of Leishmania transmitted by sandflies, while amastigotes are the diagnostic stage found within human macrophages.

questions.stem: Ziemann’s stippling of erythrocyte is caused by which species of plasmodium:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C. Malariae

Ans. C. Plasmodium vivax and ovale

 

Relapse in malaria occurs due to the reactivation of dormant liver stage forms known as hypnozoites. These are unique to: Plasmodium vivax & Plasmodium ovale
These hypnozoites remain dormant in the liver after initial infection and can reactivate weeks to months later, causing a relapse of symptoms without a new mosquito bite.
 

Other options:

 

Option A. Plasmodium vivax and falciparum: P. falciparum does not form hypnozoites. It causes recrudescence, not relapse.

 

Option B. Plasmodium ovale and falciparum: P. falciparum does not form hypnozoites. It causes recrudescence, not relapse.
    

Option D. Plasmodium vivax and malariae: P. malariae causes recrudescence, not relapse, and it can persist at low levels in blood for years, but without hypnozoites.

 

Educational Objective: 

 

Only Plasmodium vivax and ovale form dormant hypnozoites in the liver, which can reactivate to cause true relapses without re-infection.

questions.stemHtml: A 23-year-old male presented with abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea of one week duration. The following colonic biopsy is diagnostic of infection with?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Amoebiasis

 

Amoebiasis is caused by Entamoeba histolytica which invades the colonic mucosa and submucosa leading to flask-shaped ulcers that has narrow neck at the surface and broad base in the submucosa as seen in the image. 
 

The patient presents with abdominal pain, bloody diarrhoea (dysentery), fever and tenesmus.

 

Other options:

 

Option A.Giardiasis: affects the small intestine,not colon and causes fatty diarrhea, not bloody, and does not form flask-shaped ulcer

 

Option C. Enterobius: Causes perianal itching, not bloody diarrhea and rarely causes mucosal ulcers

 

Option D. Severe bacterial infection: May cause ulceration and bloody diarrhea (e.g., Shigella), but not the flask-shaped ulcers characteristic of amoebiasis.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Entamoeba histolytica causes characteristic flask-shaped ulcers in the colon with narrow necks and broad bases, distinguishing amoebiasis from other causes of bloody diarrhea.

questions.stem: Winter bottom sign in sleeping sickness refers to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Posterior cervical lymphadenopathy

 

Winterbottom sign refers to enlargement of the posterior cervical lymph nodes, which is an early clinical sign of African trypanosomiasis. It reflects lymphatic spread of the parasite after the tsetse fly bite.
 

Commonly seen in West African sleeping sickness (caused by T. brucei gambiense).
 

Other options:

 

Option A. Unilateral conjunctivitis: Seen in Chlamydia trachomatis (e.g., trachoma or inclusion conjunctivitis), not in sleeping sickness.

 

Option C. Narcolepsy: is also called as sleeping sickness causing daytime somnolence, but Winterbottom sign specifically refers to lymphadenopathy.

 

Option D. Transient erythema: Not characteristic or specific to sleeping sickness.
 

Educational Objective: 

 

Winterbottom sign refers to posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, an early diagnostic marker of African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness) following tsetse fly transmission.
